title: Job 21
paragraphs: ¹ Then Job answered and said, ² Listen carefully to what I am saying; let this be the comfort you offer me. ³ Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, go ahead and mock. ⁴ Is my complaint directed at a human being? Should I not be impatient? ⁵ Look at me and be appalled — lay your hand over your mouth.

⁶ When I think about it I am terrified, and shuddering seizes my body. ⁷ Why do the wicked go on living, growing old and increasing in power? ⁸ They see their children established around them, their offspring before their very eyes. ⁹ Their homes are safe and free from fear; God's rod does not fall on them. ¹⁰ Their bulls breed without fail; their cows calve and do not miscarry.

¹¹ They send out their children like a flock; their little ones dance about. ¹² They sing to the tambourine and lyre and make merry at the sound of the flute. ¹³ They spend their days in prosperity and go down to the grave in peace. ¹⁴ Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We don't want to know your ways. ¹⁵ What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?'

¹⁶ But their prosperity is not of their own doing — the counsel of the wicked is far from me. ¹⁷ How often does the lamp of the wicked go out? How often does disaster come upon them? How often does God mete out pain in his anger? ¹⁸ They are like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm. ¹⁹ You may say, 'God stores up a man's punishment for his children,' but let him repay the man himself, so he can know it. ²⁰ Let his own eyes see his ruin; let him drink of the Almighty's wrath.

²¹ For what does he care about his household after him, when his months are cut short? ²² Can anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges even those on high? ²³ One person dies in the fullness of his strength, completely secure and at ease, ²⁴ his body well nourished, the marrow of his bones moist. ²⁵ Another dies in bitterness of soul, never having tasted anything good.

²⁶ They lie down alike in the dust, and worms cover them both. ²⁷ I know exactly what you are thinking, and the schemes you devise against me. ²⁸ You say, 'Where is the great man's house? Where are the tents where the wicked lived?' ²⁹ Have you never questioned those who travel the roads? Have you not paid attention to their accounts? ³⁰ The wicked man is spared when disaster comes; he is delivered on the day of wrath.

³¹ Who will confront him to his face about his deeds? Who will repay him for what he has done? ³² He is carried to his grave, and watch is kept over his tomb. ³³ The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows after him, and those who went before him are beyond counting. ³⁴ So how can you offer me such empty comfort? Your answers are nothing but lies.
